note: quince#83 constraint 3, and it is the only thing standing between the suppression and a lost signal. `kind=post-merge` is SUPPRESSED from the wake decision, so the case that must never carry that label is a PR somebody actually said something on after it merged — a reviewer noting a follow-up, an Operator ruling in a thread, a correction. THE THIRD CLAUSE IS WHAT PROTECTS IT: the label needs `MERGED` at the previous observation AND `updatedAt` moved AND nothing in activity newer, and a comment lands in activity with a newer timestamp, so the event is attributed and never labelled. Dropping that clause would turn a conservative inference into the guess the filer warned against, and this fixture is what fails if anybody does. PR 703 is the comment; PR 704 is its partner in the SAME observation with nothing newer, so one tick produces both a suppressed event and a woken one — a fixture where only the surviving case appeared would pass against a build that had stopped labelling anything at all.
